The switch to Decimal with ROUND_HALF_UP is the right fix for the real bug: float `:.1f` rounds 1.25 to 1.2 instead of 1.3. The carry logic (1048575 → "1.0 MB") is also correct. But the added rule "always round up (ROUND_UP) for values in [1, 2)" is not in the docstring. It was reverse-engineered to pass `test_upload_limit_label`.

That test conflicts with the documented spec. 1_500_000 / 1024**2 ≈ 1.4305 MB, and the docstring (binary units, one decimal place, halves rounded up) gives "1.4 MB", not "1.5 MB". The "1.5 MB" matches decimal megabytes (1.5e6 / 1e6), so the test may have been written with SI units in mind.

The special case breaks other inputs. For example, 1034 bytes (1.0098 KB) now shows as "1.1 KB" instead of "1.0 KB", and rounding behaves differently on each side of 2.0. The web UI and the weekly usage emails share this formatter, so both would change. The PR description also invents a reason for this rule ("makes sense for a storage quota system") that nobody asked for.

Please drop the [1, 2) branch and use ROUND_HALF_UP everywhere. Then raise the `test_upload_limit_label` conflict with the requester and the storage team so they can decide whether the test or the spec should change, instead of hiding the conflict behind a special case.
